abilities.name: leitvia/add-media

abilities.description: Adds an image to the media library from a URL of this site or as Base64 data up to 5 MB, with alt text or marked as decorative. It also takes a WebVTT file with captions for a video (.vtt, UTF-8, starts with WEBVTT, no alt text) and a video hosted on this site, MP4 (H.264) or WebM up to 50 MB, with poster and caption instead of alt text (poster_file names a poster image that still waits in the same package), and a PDF up to 5 MB (.pdf, with the PDF signature at its start) with a title that says what the document is, without alt text; no other document type. It needs the right to upload files. URLs of other hosts are rejected; nothing is fetched from them. base_hash is empty. With replace the file takes the place of the file of an attachment under the same ID and address, for a new cut of a video or a corrected PDF; a person applies that. Images already in the library are used by their ID in compose-page and update-block, a WebVTT file by its ID in tracks of update-block, a video by its ID in the field video of update-block, a PDF by its URL from the result or leitvia/list-media in url or add_link of update-block.

abilities.name: leitvia/apply-recipe
abilities.label: Apply recipe
abilities.description: Sets up the site from a recipe of leitvia/list-recipes: content model and building blocks, token set, style variation, header and footer, pages from patterns, navigation, reading settings and options that save data. Each part runs through its own ability with the autonomy level of its area; what may not go live lands in one change package, and with a package key everything does. Settings that point to a page waiting in that package (front page, privacy policy page) are set when the package is applied. Pages that exist, and variation, header, footer and navigation changed since a recipe wrote them, are kept, as is the variation while a token set is active, so the recipe can run again after the package was applied. parts, pages and buildingBlocks limit the run to a selection, and slugs gives recipe pages other addresses; navigation and footer then link only the pages that are on the site or come in this run, and a navigation without any of them waits. dryRun reports what would change without writing. Review the package with leitvia/get-package. With settle, a person (manage_options, not the agent role) in the admin, neither signed in with an application password nor calling over MCP, who runs it without a package key applies what collects at once: applied lists the packages applied in full, which can be rolled back in the Inbox, and partial the packages applied in part, with their errors. abilities.name: leitvia/audit-site
abilities.label: Audit site
abilities.description: Runs the content checks (headings, alt text, link text, #anchor links, block validity, unregistered blocks, tokens, contrast, one h1 and landmarks) over published content, at most 20 posts per call in ID order. Also reports classic content without blocks, deprecated patterns, preset slugs missing from the active tokens, internal links that lead to no page or to the old address of a renamed post, links that lead nowhere (empty href, # without target) on the rendered page outside content and template parts, with their class, pages that look like legal texts without a page kind, placeholders left on legal pages (square brackets such as [Organization name] and sentences that say they are a placeholder), and uneven motion (leitvia/motion): leitviaMotion other than the site setting, fade and rise on one page, more than one kind of striking effect, more than 3 striking or 6 animated blocks. The first page (after 0) also returns site: an error when the site is closed to search engines outside a local or staging site, a warning when Gravity Forms loads a captcha from another host (a captcha add-on or a reCAPTCHA field), an error per header or footer part with such links, warnings for a missing imprint, contact or editorial page while there are posts, and for the latest 20 news posts without a featured image of at least 1200 px width or whose author has no biography. Pass next as after for the following page; next is null at the end.

after.description: Start after this post ID, the next value of the previous call.

abilities.name: leitvia/check-composition
abilities.label: Check composition
abilities.description: Scores a page against the composition rules of the contract: pass pattern slugs in page order (block:<ID> for a Lab pattern; only approved ones count as known), or a post ID to read the sections of a saved page from metadata.patternName. A saved page counts as built: the ground each section sets (backgroundColor, block style Inverse) instead of the tone of its pattern, and the side of its media (block style Media right). With slugs, name both yourself: tones for the sections an edit will give another ground, mirrored for those it will give the block style Media right, each by 0-based index. Text, lists, images, galleries and accordions between the sections are running text and no finding. A section with a video, a gallery or a wide image is a break and stands outside the density run. With frame (or the frame a saved page was composed for) the page also needs a section of every kind the page frame requires (missingSection, 10 points) and is told about the kinds it recommends (recommendedSection, no points); both carry the kind and the index after the last section, and their suggestions name patterns to add. Returns the findings (rule, 0-based section index, for a post the block ID, and what to do), the score from 100 down, the minimum score for autonomous writes and per finding up to three patterns that would fix it. For a post also unregistered: block types that render nothing.

abilities.name: leitvia/compose-page
abilities.label: Compose page
abilities.description: Creates a page from patterns in the order of a page frame of the contract, or rebuilds an existing page (post). With post all its sections are replaced in one step, and the checks (one h1, structure, composition) see only the finished page, never a state in between. Plan it with leitvia/plan-page first; base_hash is empty for a new page and the hash of leitvia/get-page-outline for post. The page remembers its frame, so check-composition counts the sections the frame requires (hub, audience) or recommends (service). Per section texts (also quote citations and details summaries), links, images, captions, catalog attributes, an HTML anchor and the columns of a grid at block IDs of the pattern outline can change, remove and repeat take blocks from a parent or add copies, for fewer or more entries than the pattern, and insert adds a block of leitvia/list-blocks after a block, given as name with attributes, anchor and inner blocks, never as markup (text with link_text and url for a link inside it, table for the cells of a table, any number of list items as inner); table fills the head, rows and foot of a core/table or leitvia/comparison-table accessibly; a text that would drop a link is refused. Edits apply in order. Each section keeps metadata.patternName (core/block/<ID> for a Lab pattern). Unknown patterns are rejected with a pointer to leitvia/list-patterns, deprecated ones with their replacement, Lab patterns that are not approved (also through a part) with leitvia_pattern_not_approved. abilities.name: leitvia/get-package
abilities.label: Get change package
abilities.description: Returns a change package with its operations: status, the post each applied operation wrote, conflicts and, for open operations, a block diff against the current state (per block added, removed, moved or changed with text before and after and the changed attributes). applied.post is the ID a new post got, applied.hash its hash after the write.

id.description: Change package ID.

state.description: open, applied, partial, rejected or rolled_back.

operations.description: Number of operations per status: open, conflict, applied, rolled_back.

items.description: The operations with status, target, findings and, for open ones, the block diff.

abilities.name: leitvia/get-page-outline
abilities.label: Get page outline
abilities.description: Returns a post as a compact block tree: per block the ID, name, pattern, the first 80 characters of text (with text_hash of the whole text when it is longer), the link targets of the block itself (links, only when it has any), for image and cover blocks the image with attachment ID, alt text and decorative mark, size, hash and children. shortcodes: unhandled shortcodes per block. Blocks without a stable ID have a path ID such as p:0.2.1 until the next save. Use the document hash as base_hash for changes and get-block for full attributes.

text_hash.description: Only when text was cut: the first 16 hex characters of the SHA-256 of the whole text, tags stripped, entities decoded, white space collapsed to single spaces and trimmed.

image.description: Image of an image or cover block: attachment ID (0 outside the media library), alt text (null without alt attribute) and the decorative mark.

shortcodes.description: Only when present: name and block of each.

abilities.name: leitvia/get-pattern
abilities.label: Get pattern
abilities.description: Returns one pattern of the theme or of Leitvia Studio with its markup, metadata and the first 20 posts and templates that use it (more is true when there are further ones). Template patterns come with their templateTypes.

slug.description: Pattern slug from list-patterns, for example leitvia/hero-split-image, or block:<ID> for a Lab pattern.

abilities.name: leitvia/get-product
abilities.label: Get product
abilities.description: Returns one product or variation: texts, images with alt text, categories and tags with their hash, attributes, price (read only), tax and shipping class, stock status, merchandising and the hash to use as base_hash. No sales, order or customer figures.

product.description: Product or variation ID from leitvia/list-products.

abilities.name: leitvia/get-seo
abilities.label: Get SEO data
abilities.description: Returns the SEO data of posts, pages and entries from the active SEO plugin. Supported are Yoast SEO, Rank Math, SEOPress and The SEO Framework. Per item: title, meta description, canonical, noindex, nofollow, Open Graph title, description and image, focus keyword and schema type. schema_type is the article type Leitvia Studio prints for a post (NewsArticle or BlogPosting), null where it prints none; structure holds the page frame, hub, service and offerings of a page (leitvia/set-page-structure). indexable says whether the site is open to search engines, news_sitemap is the address of the news sitemap of Leitvia Studio or null, organization holds the details of leitvia/set-organization: type, name, url, address, phone, email, founding date, founder, start year and holder of the copyright line, area served, opening hours, profiles and aggregate_rating. redirects lists the rows of leitvia/set-redirects, llms whether llms.txt was asked for (requested) and is served (enabled), held_back why a requested file is not served (site closed to search engines, SEO plugin), its address, summary, extra pages and whether AI crawlers may crawl (leitvia/set-llms). An empty value means the plugin falls back to its template. defaults holds what WordPress itself would print and a description suggested from the excerpt; without an SEO plugin plugin names Leitvia Studio, with an unsupported one seo is null, and notice says why. hash is the base_hash of leitvia/update-seo. IDs that are no readable content come back under skipped.

posts.description: IDs of posts, pages or entries from leitvia/list-content.

abilities.name: leitvia/get-site-health
abilities.label: Get site health
abilities.description: Returns the versions of WordPress, PHP, the theme and the plugins and the updates WordPress knows of, read from its last update check; nothing is requested. mcp says whether MCP clients reach the server of Leitvia Studio (ready), its address (url) and, when not, why (reason, such as the plugin MCP Adapter missing): report that to the person and go on over the REST API. Needs a user who may view the Site Health checks, usually an administrator, or the agent role.

abilities.name: leitvia/get-tokens
abilities.label: Get tokens
abilities.description: Returns the active design tokens as a DTCG document (of the active token set, else of the current global styles), the token sets with their status, the active style variations, whether the global styles drifted from the active set, the contrast findings of the current palette and the hash of the global styles, the base_hash of leitvia/activate-token-set and leitvia/set-variation.

hash.description: Hash of the global styles; empty while the theme has none saved.

abilities.name: leitvia/import-post
abilities.label: Import post
abilities.description: Imports one post, page or entry of the content model from another site for a migration: source is its old address, content its HTML. The HTML becomes core blocks; shortcodes of WPBakery and Impreza (vc_row, vc_column, vc_column_text, vc_single_image, vc_btn, us_text, us_btn and others with text) become blocks, every other shortcode leaves only its text. Only shortcodes count: those registered here, of core or of a known page builder or form plugin; any other text in square brackets stays, and inside pre and code nothing changes. Images of the source host (and of media_hosts) are loaded into the media library once, the featured image from featured_image.url too; links to the source host become paths of this site, heading levels below the title close their gaps. author takes a user ID, login or email of a user of this site; parent an ID or parent_source, the old address of an imported parent. A second call with the same source updates that post instead of creating a new one. The write follows leitvia/create-content or leitvia/update-content with their checks and autonomy. Script, style, noscript, template and form elements go with their content (report.removed counts them per tag); report lists the loaded images and everything that did not carry over. dry_run shows the block markup and the report without loading or writing anything.

source.description: Address of the post on the old site, http or https; the key that makes a second import update the same post.

post_type.description: post, page or a post type of the content model.

title.description: Title of the post on the old site, without the name of the site.

content.description: HTML of the post as the old site stores it, shortcodes included.

date.description: Date in the time zone of the site, YYYY-MM-DD or YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.

author.description: User ID, login or email of an existing user of this site; without a match the post belongs to the user who writes it and report.author says so.

author_name.description: Name of an author of the old site who has no account here, as the old site showed it: the post shows it as its author name and in its structured data (Person), and no user is created. Written on every import, so a second one can add or correct it; leitvia/update-content takes it too.

author_page.description: ID of a published page about the author of author_name, such as an about or team page: the author name links to it and the structured data (Person) names it as url, which Google News asks for. 0 removes it.

parent_source.description: Old address of the parent, imported before with leitvia/import-post or waiting in the open package with the same package key; instead of parent. Without such a parent the import is rejected, never placed at the top level. A second import with it moves the post under that parent.

terms.description: Terms by taxonomy, such as {"category": ["News"], "post_tag": ["events", 12]}: IDs as numbers, names or slugs as text. They replace the terms of that taxonomy.

url.description: Address of the image on the old site.

images.description: Attachment ID on the old site => address of that image, for image shortcodes such as vc_single_image image="123".

media_hosts.description: More hosts images may come from, such as the CDN of the old site.

seo.description: SEO title and meta description of the old site, written as by leitvia/update-seo.

package.description: Key of the task: every import of a migration with the same key goes into one change package.

mode.description: What happened: live (written and visible), draft (written as a draft), package (nothing written yet: the change waits in a change package until a person applies it in the inbox; leitvia/get-package shows it), unchanged (the target already had this state).

level.description: Autonomy level of the area that decided the mode.

hash.description: Hash of the target after the call, the base_hash of the next change on it. A change that waits in a package writes nothing, so the hash is the one the target already had, and the next change of the same package sends it too; empty only for a new post that waits in a package.

package.description: ID of the change package the change waits in, or that leitvia/rollback undoes a live write with; 0 for none.

snapshot.description: ID of the snapshot of the state before the write; 0 for none.

slug_changed.description: The slug asked for (requested) is taken or reserved, so the address uses slug instead, on publishing at the latest.

applied.description: For a list of items: the package that holds what went live, for leitvia/rollback; 0 for none.

items.description: For a list of items: the result per item in their order, or code, message, reason and target of its rejection.

abilities.name: leitvia/insert-section
abilities.label: Insert section
abilities.description: Inserts sections into the content of an existing post, page or entry, or moves one of its top-level sections; the rest of the content stays as it is. sections takes patterns with edits as in leitvia/compose-page, with the same checks; move takes the ID of a top-level section of the post instead. The place is after or before a top-level section (block ID or path ID from the outline) or position start or end; without a place the sections go to the end. An anchor of a new section must be unique on the whole page. Read the post with leitvia/get-page-outline first and send its hash as base_hash. leitvia/remove-section takes a section out, leitvia/replace-pattern gives one another pattern.

sections.description: Sections of the page in order, each a pattern with optional edits at block IDs of its outline.

pattern.description: Pattern slug such as leitvia/hero-split-image, or block:<ID> for a Lab pattern.

block.description: Block ID or path ID from the outline.

text.description: Plain text of a paragraph, heading, list item or button, the citation of a quote or the summary of a details block.

link_text.description: Part of text that stays linked when the text holds a link, such as the mail address in a contact line; with url it links that part of a text without a link. Without it the link stays around its old text, and a text without that is refused unless the link only points to #.

url.description: Link of a button, or of the one link in a paragraph, heading or list item (mailto: and tel: work too). "" removes the saved link of a button whose link a binding fills; the binding stays.

add_link.description: New link around a passage of a paragraph, heading, list item, citation or summary, as text with the exact words and url. Other links and inline formatting stay; the first place outside a link counts.

text.description: The exact words of the passage to link, without markup.

url.description: Target of the link (mailto: and tel: work too).

caption.description: Caption of an image, video, audio, gallery, table or embed as plain text; empty removes it.

anchor.description: HTML anchor (id) of a block with the support anchor, unique on the page, such as contact-form for links to #contact-form; empty or null removes it.

table.description: All cells of a core/table or leitvia/comparison-table as plain text: head (the column headers), rows (each as long as head) and for core/table foot (a highlighted closing row, such as a total). The table is rebuilt accessibly: column headers with scope col, the first cell of each row as row header with scope row (row_headers false for none). The caption goes in caption of the same edit. On small screens core tables scroll inside a focusable region, the comparison table turns into cards.

rows.description: The rows in order, each a list of cells as long as head.

columns.description: Column count of a grid or a gallery: a group or post template with the layout grid, such as the cards of a teaser pattern, or a gallery block. Four cards take 2: with 4 a narrower window still wraps to 3 + 1.

id.description: Attachment ID of the image, from leitvia/list-media or leitvia/add-media.

alt.description: Alt text of the image here. Left out, the image keeps its alt text from the media library; an image without one needs alt or decorative true.

video.description: Video of a core/video from the media library: sets src, poster, controls and preload none, also on a video block that is still empty. caption and attributes with tracks or align go in the same edit. Text tracks the block has stay; send tracks when the new video has other captions.

id.description: Attachment ID of the video, from leitvia/list-media or leitvia/add-media.

poster.description: Attachment ID of the image that shows before the video plays. Left out, the poster the video got in leitvia/add-media.

remove.description: Removes the block from its parent, for a section with fewer entries than the pattern. Later edits of the list count from the result, so work from the last block to the first.

repeat.description: Number of copies to add right after the block, for a section with more entries than the pattern. Later edits reach the copies by the IDs they get.

move.description: Block ID or path ID of a block with the same parent: the block moves right after it, or before it with position before, such as a button above a heading. Later edits count from the new order.

position.description: With insert or move only: after (the default) or before the block of the edit, or of move.

insert.description: A new block right after the block (or before it with position before), in the same parent, such as leitvia/form-errors with gravityforms/form inside or leitvia/consent-embed; a static block starts from the example of the catalog. Later edits reach it and its inner blocks by the IDs they get.

block.description: Name of a block from leitvia/list-blocks, such as leitvia/consent-embed, or core/paragraph, core/heading, core/separator or core/site-logo. Inner blocks may also be other blocks that render on the server, such as gravityforms/form.

text.description: Plain text of a new paragraph, heading, list item or button.

link_text.description: With text and url: the part of text that becomes the link, such as the mail address in a contact line.

url.description: Link of a new button, or with link_text of the link in a new paragraph, heading or list item (mailto: and tel: work too).

table.description: All cells of a core/table or leitvia/comparison-table as plain text: head (the column headers), rows (each as long as head) and for core/table foot (a highlighted closing row, such as a total). The table is rebuilt accessibly: column headers with scope col, the first cell of each row as row header with scope row (row_headers false for none). The caption goes in caption of the same edit. On small screens core tables scroll inside a focusable region, the comparison table turns into cards.

rows.description: The rows in order, each a list of cells as long as head.

attributes.description: Attributes from leitvia/list-blocks, checked as in leitvia/update-block.

anchor.description: HTML anchor (id) of a block with the support anchor, unique on the page, such as contact-form for links to #contact-form; empty or null removes it.

inner.description: Inner blocks in order, in place of those of the catalog example.

move.description: Block ID or path ID of a top-level section of the post that moves to the place, instead of sections.

after.description: Block ID or path ID of the top-level section the new sections follow.

before.description: Block ID or path ID of the top-level section the new sections precede.

position.description: Start or end of the content, instead of after or before.

base_hash.description: Hash of the target as last read; empty for a new object.

package.description: Key of the task: a write with a key always goes into the change package of that key, even where the autonomy would allow it live, and operations with the same key share that package.

mode.description: What happened: live (written and visible), draft (written as a draft), package (nothing written yet: the change waits in a change package until a person applies it in the inbox; leitvia/get-package shows it), unchanged (the target already had this state).

level.description: Autonomy level of the area that decided the mode.

hash.description: Hash of the target after the call, the base_hash of the next change on it. A change that waits in a package writes nothing, so the hash is the one the target already had, and the next change of the same package sends it too; empty only for a new post that waits in a package.

package.description: ID of the change package the change waits in, or that leitvia/rollback undoes a live write with; 0 for none.

snapshot.description: ID of the snapshot of the state before the write; 0 for none.

abilities.name: leitvia/list-blocks
abilities.label: List blocks
abilities.description: Returns the block catalog of Leitvia Studio and its add-ons with attribute schema and usage rules, and the registered block styles of every block, core blocks included, by block name; a style is set as the class is-style-<name>. With post_type only the blocks the editor allows for that post type.

post_type.description: Limit to the blocks allowed for this post type.

description.description: Translated description of what the block does.

parent.description: Blocks this block must be a direct child of, null for anywhere.

ancestor.description: Blocks this block must be inside at any depth, null for anywhere.

supports.description: Supports of block.json an agent may use: align, anchor, color, spacing, typography, dimensions, border, shadow, layout, html, multiple, reusable, inserter, interactivity. Their attributes (className, style, backgroundColor and so on) are not listed under attributes.

attributes.description: JSON schema of the block attributes from block.json. A property with source is stored in the block markup, not in the block comment; rich-text is a string of HTML. leitviaAnimation (none, fade, rise, stagger, zoom, slide-start, slide-end, wipe-up, wipe-start, blur, mask, parallax) and leitviaMotion (subtle, bold) are on every block, core blocks included, except blocks without markup of their own, the navigation and leitvia/reveal; their descriptions say when they fit.

innerBlocks.description: Blocks allowed directly inside: allowedBlocks of block.json, otherwise the catalog blocks that name this block as parent. null when block.json sets no limit.

example.description: Saved markup of a block that keeps its content in HTML: write the block like this, an empty or self-closing block renders nothing. Blocks that render on the server have none; their attributes are enough.

usage.description: When to use the block. Required for Studio blocks, optional for add-on blocks.

owner.description: Slug of the add-on that registered the block in the Studio blocks registry, core for core blocks.

extension.description: Core blocks only: what Studio changes about the block.

styles.description: Block styles by block name, from block.json and register_block_style(), each with name and label.

abilities.name: leitvia/list-building-blocks
abilities.label: List building blocks
abilities.description: Lists the building blocks of add-ons: name, title, description, whether the site has them, their post types and taxonomies, the patterns that show them and the number of sample entries. Add one with leitvia/add-building-block.

abilities.name: leitvia/list-content
abilities.label: List content
abilities.description: Lists posts, pages and entries of the content model, newest first, with hash, terms and the open package that waits for each. Per item: ID, type, status, title, slug, date, modified, author (ID) and author_name as visitors see it, excerpt, terms, fields, rows of repeaters, link, hash and package. Filter by type, status, search text, modified since and published after a date. Only content agents may read; no comments, users or form entries.

post_type.description: One post type; empty for all content types.

since.description: Date in the time zone of the site, YYYY-MM-DD or YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.

after.description: Date in the time zone of the site, YYYY-MM-DD or YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.

abilities.name: leitvia/list-media
abilities.label: List media
abilities.description: Lists the media library, newest first: ID, URL, file name, MIME type, file size in bytes, alt text, width, height and hash (the base_hash for leitvia/set-alt-text). Filter by IDs (include, in their order, for example the images of a gallery), by search text in title, caption and file name, MIME type (image, image/png or application/pdf) and uploaded after a date.

include.description: Only these attachment IDs, in this order. IDs that are no media of the library are left out.

search.description: Text in the title, caption or file name.

after.description: Date in the time zone of the site, YYYY-MM-DD or YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.

abilities.name: leitvia/list-packages
abilities.label: List change packages
abilities.description: Lists your change packages, newest first: ID, title, key, state (open, applied, partial, rejected, rolled_back), operations per status and a preview link.

state.description: open, applied, partial, rejected or rolled_back.

operations.description: Number of operations per status: open, conflict, applied, rolled_back.

abilities.name: leitvia/list-patterns
abilities.label: List patterns
abilities.description: Lists the patterns of the theme, of Leitvia Studio and of its add-ons (source addon) with composition metadata, image slots, when to use and avoid them, lab status and the replacement of deprecated ones, followed by the Lab patterns (slug block:<ID>, source lab) with their lab status, version and document hash, and the composition of the theme pattern they vary. Only approved Lab patterns count as known in check-composition. provides names the section kinds of the contract a pattern fills (sectionKinds, as page frames require them), continues the patterns it continues as one section. Filter by role, tone, layout, provides or category; at most 50 per page. Markup and usage come from get-pattern.

role.description: Filter by this value of the composition metadata.

tone.description: Filter by this value of the composition metadata.

layout.description: Filter by this value of the composition metadata.

provides.description: Filter by a section kind of the contract (sectionKinds), for example faq or answer.

abilities.name: leitvia/list-product-attributes
abilities.label: List product attributes
abilities.description: Lists the global product attributes with their values and hash. Per attribute ID, name, slug (taxonomy pa_*) and sort order, per value ID, name and slug, in the order the shop shows them. Attributes a single product defines for itself are part of leitvia/get-product.

abilities.name: leitvia/list-product-reviews
abilities.label: List product reviews
abilities.description: Lists product reviews with rating and hash, 20 per page, oldest first; per review ID, product, author name, date, text, rating (1 to 5, 0 for none), verified owner and status. unrated lists only reviews without a rating; unrated_total counts them. Without the capability of the reviews screen of WooCommerce (moderate_comments) only approved reviews of published products, which visitors see anyway; status in the output names the status listed. No email address, IP address or user account of a reviewer.

abilities.name: leitvia/list-products
abilities.label: List products
abilities.description: Lists the products of the shop, 20 per page, with title, type, status, price (read only), stock status, featured flag and hash, plus all product categories with their hash. Filter by category or search text. Orders, coupons and customers are never listed.

abilities.name: leitvia/list-recipes
abilities.label: List recipes
abilities.description: Lists the site recipes of Leitvia Studio and its add-ons with owner, pages and whether the plugins they require are active.

abilities.name: leitvia/plan-page
abilities.label: Plan page
abilities.description: Proposes a page for a goal and content points: page frame, template, the patterns in page order with role, slot, text lengths and the points each section carries, and the composition score. Without AI the plan follows the page frames, examples and composition rules of the contract and is the same for the same input; it leaves out patterns that need images while the media library has none, post teasers below three published posts and proof or offer patterns, which carry facts of the person, and patterns the inserter hides, and plans a shop home from the home page of the shop recipe. A point that starts with the role, slot or area of a section and a colon (Hero: ...) lands on that section. With ai set to true the AI connector the site owner set up in WordPress refines it; the goal, the points and pattern names with their metadata are sent to that provider. Writes nothing; build the page with leitvia/compose-page.

goal.description: What the page is for, in a sentence; a page frame type it names (home, service) picks the frame.

frame.description: Type of a page frame; without it the frame named in the goal, else home.

ai.description: Refine the plan through the AI connector of the site. Sends the goal, the points and pattern names to that provider.

abilities.name: leitvia/preview-token-set
abilities.label: Preview token set
abilities.description: Returns a signed address that shows the site with a token set, for that request only. The page looks as the activation of the set would make it (colors, fonts, sizes, widths); nothing changes for visitors and nothing is saved. Open it in a browser or screenshot tool without signing in; it expires after an hour, carries noindex and is not cached. Compare style variants this way instead of activating them. The set ID comes from leitvia/get-tokens or leitvia/create-token-set; path is an address of this site such as /about/, the front page when empty.

set.description: Token set ID from the sets of leitvia/get-tokens or from leitvia/create-token-set.

abilities.name: leitvia/reject-package
abilities.label: Discard change package
abilities.description: Discards an open or partly applied change package. Its open operations stay unwritten and their waiting files are deleted, operations already applied stay. Use it for your own package when a run took a wrong turn; users with manage_options may discard any package. The package stays with the state rejected and the audit log keeps the call. It cannot be undone, so build the change again with a new package key.

abilities.name: leitvia/replace-pattern
abilities.label: Replace pattern
abilities.description: Replaces top-level sections of one post with another pattern. Without pattern the sections that use a deprecated pattern (metadata.patternName) get the replacement the contract names, all of them or the one given by block; leitvia/audit-site reports such posts, and a section without replacement is rejected with leitvia_no_replacement. With pattern the one section given by block gets that pattern, any approved one of leitvia/list-patterns, with edits at block IDs of its outline as in leitvia/compose-page (text, link, image, caption, catalog attributes such as the level of a heading, anchor, columns of a grid, remove, repeat and insert): so a section of an existing page changes its pattern. Texts and button links of the old section move over in order per block type (carry false keeps the texts of the pattern), then the edits apply and win; the HTML anchor of the old section does not move over, set it again with an anchor edit. The base hash is the hash of the post from leitvia/get-page-outline.

abilities.name: leitvia/set-redirects
abilities.label: Set redirects
abilities.description: Sets the redirects of moved and removed addresses, for a migration or a new structure. Rows of from, a path of this site such as /old-page/, status and to. A from with a query, such as /?p=45 or /?attachment_id=123 of an old site, matches only that query (in any order of its parameters) and comes before the row of its bare path; a from without a query matches its path with any query. status 301 (the default) moves for good, 302 for a while; both need to, a path of this site or an https address. status 410 says the page is gone for good (search engines drop it faster than a 404) and takes no to; the visitor sees the 404 page of the theme. The list replaces the saved one (at most 1000 rows, read the current one with leitvia/get-seo); an empty list removes all. A request of a from path gets its answer before the page loads; a trailing slash and the case do not matter. Rows that lead back to a path they passed (a loop) are refused, as are the start page as from, a target equal to its from and a 410 with a target. Inactive while an SEO plugin is active, which brings its own redirects. base_hash is empty. Like every setting it waits in a change package for a person.

abilities.name: leitvia/update-block
abilities.label: Update block
abilities.description: Changes one block found by its ID or path ID: attributes from the block catalog and the level of a heading, the text of a paragraph, heading, list item or button, the citation of a quote, the summary of a details block, the link of a button or of the one link in a text (link_text names the linked part, also for a text that gets its first link), the cells of a core/table or leitvia/comparison-table with table (head, rows, foot), or the image of an image or cover block with alt text. video sets the video of a core/video from the media library by its ID, with poster, controls and preload none, also on the empty video of a pattern. add_link sets a new link on a passage of a text, caption the caption of an image, video, audio, gallery, table or embed, anchor the HTML anchor of a block with the support anchor (unique on the page), columns the column count of a grid (group or post template with the layout grid) or of a gallery. A heading or paragraph takes fontSize with a font size of the tokens, a group with a light ground takes backgroundColor surface or surface-alt, each as attribute. label changes the name for screen readers (aria-label) of a slider, announcement bar or accessibility bar. A timeline entry takes date, dateLabel and heading as attributes. Attributes that a static block keeps in its markup, such as prefix, value, suffix and label of a counter, change like any other. query of a core/query merges into its settings. tracks of a core/video replaces its text tracks: each names a WebVTT file from leitvia/add-media by id, with kind, srclang and label. A spotlight point moves with attributes x and y in percent. The effect on scroll (leitviaAnimation, leitviaMotion) changes on every block that has it, core blocks and saved markup included, since only the block comment changes. Static markup is rebuilt with the HTML API; changes it cannot rebuild safely are rejected with leitvia_static_markup. Read the post with leitvia/get-page-outline first and send its hash as base_hash; get-block shows the current attributes. For several text changes in one post use leitvia/update-content.
